title: High effort ai gamedevs deserve some respect.
author: Maidforblood
selftext:
I've seen some posts that was a little talked  about with ai hate abd ai game dev hate teain due to low quality effort "games" been seeing from steam fest lately.  Bit i seen some really good and promising game dev project using ai as a tool to potentially make your idea come to life, given with enough effort you can go far and no one would care if you use ai to make games ad long ss your project hsd passion and had great effort put into it. People will still appreciate game dev in some form with genuine quality. Just remember what you asked for when using ai tools. 

As a fellow game dev. I put passion and effort into maid for blood. I am currently doing 2 maid character reworks. Still alot to be done before release on my steam page.

comments.author: talamakina
comments.body: Honestly, I don't even knock on "low effort" devs. Most are just exploring gamedev, or are just learning.

replies.body: The learning gamedev part i agree with. I used to mess around with ai tools before committing to a project i have vision to make out of it.

replies.author: talamakina
replies.body:
Now lets keep in mind, there are projects out there that are straight up ripoffs or clones or REA artifacts from malicious devs stealing published builds. Thats a fact.

A gamedev, given unique constraints (ie, have to make the game in under 2 weeks, and have it hyper polished as much as it can be) now has no bar to a playable build : the bar to entry is now about Gamers willing to accept your art style.

Its a unique "schism" playing in real time.

comments.author: Substantial-Ad-1546
comments.body:
There are folks within the anti circles who like to collapse all AI-assisted development into "prompt in -> product out" with no skill required or creativity involved, and they can be highly resistant to new information. It's okay to ignore them. I am willing to discuss my process when it's met with genuine curiosity, but I do not owe these people infinite attention or time spent defending my process, and neither do you. If they want to hold onto their grudges and misconceptions, let them. If you put your heart into the work, the accumulation of human-made decisions and human taste will shine through and will be clearly distinguishable from one-shotted/careless work, and people will appreciate it accordingly.

I figure, it's relatively early on yet, new technology is often met with hostility, give people time to learn about the different ways of approaching AI-assisted development. In the meantime, make the thing because you want to make the thing and ignore the hate mob. You're not making this for them anyway, you're making it because it's the thing you want to see in the world and the experience that you want to share with people.

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
So I generally agree with your sentiment. So I was excited to check out what this high effort Maid Of Blood game was.. 

And it's a vampire survivors clone... Same picking power ups as you level up, same picking different characters with powers as vamp survivors. The UI is very cluttered and each UI element is a different style. The walking animations don't match move speed. None of the characters arms move at all and are stuck down by their side.

I mean even something as the setting button on the top right during gameplay is not centered properly. 

I'm not trying to sound harsh here. But if you release this on steam without major changes the reviews are going to brutal and it will be directly lumped into the AI slop category in the players minds.

comments.author: SingleAttitude8
comments.body:
The problem is that AI is so hated in many communities (for various reasons) that any association with AI brings up negatives automatically.

As a society we haven't yet had time to work through all the nuances, and haven't had the time to come up with more balanced views on AI like you suggest. 

It's no different in principle (although differnet in practice) to many other forms of 'abuse' or discrimination. Remember, it wasn't long ago in many modern western societies that women and ethnic backgrounds did not get as much respect as others. 

What gives me hope is that often the most powerful hate voices come from ignorance, and when people improve their understanding, so the ignorance often goes away, as does the hate. 

I will admit that personally about 6-12 months ago I was very against AI, however I've come to better understand the various dimensions and viewpoints of AI, and today I'm more balanced. 

Yet I know it takes a huge amount of effort to reflect thoroughly on this stuff, and not everyone has the time and willingness to do so. So I think we're just in a transition period while we wait for society to collectively do the thinking and come up with more holistic views.

In the meantime, best not to lose any sleep over it.

replies.author: Neon_Camouflage
replies.body:
>What gives me hope is that often the most powerful hate voices come from ignorance, and when people improve their understanding, so the ignorance often goes away, as does the hate.

Also the simple matter of personal convenience. As better AI integration occurs over a wider variety of products and services, people will no longer be able to so easily maintain the position of simply ignoring it because they don't code or want AI art. Right now being full anti-AI is a free position of moral superiority for many people, they don't actually lose out on anything so holding that position costs them nothing.

Once people see that it can be personally useful to them, I expect quite a lot of them will quietly hop off their high horse and carry on as though they were never railing against it to begin with. The anti-AI crowd will eventually resemble the current vegan crowd, a small minority actually willing to put in effort and suffer inconvenience to maintain their moral position.
